title: Vendor risk briefing: criteria, scoring rubric, and review notes
overview: Working doc: compact briefing template for internal risk review meetings with vendors that provide inference or model hosting. Purpose: give a repeatable, lightweight rubric to surface high-risk items quickly and capture meeting notes/action items. This is intentionally pragmatic (not a full questionnaire).
assessment_objectives: 1) Determine immediate blockers for onboarding (legal, encryption, data flows). 2) Produce a 0-100 risk score for go/no-go and required mitigations. 3) Capture follow-ups and assign owners for gating items.
scoring_rubric:
Score ranges and weightings we used in the pilot (changeable):
- Data handling & residency (weight 30): 0=full access to raw prompt+logs, 50=pseudonymization + limited export, 100=no retention of prompt data beyond ephemeral cache.
- Key management & secrets (weight 20): 0=no KMS/HSM support or shared keys, 50=customer-managed keys with limited integration, 100=full BYOK + HSM + rotation documented.
- Model/artifact licensing & weights (weight 10): 0=unclear licensing, 50=restricted reuse only, 100=permissive + provenance.
- Observability & audit (weight 15): 0=no audit logs or tamper proofing, 50=basic logs retained short-term, 100=full immutable audit trail + log export.
- Availability & fallback (weight 10): 0=no SLA, 50=best-effort, 100=SLA + multi-region fallback.
- Vendor security posture (weight 15): 0=no pen test evidence or SOC reports, 50=partial evidence (pen test w/ gaps), 100=SOC2 + pen test results + remediation plan.
Final risk score = weighted sum normalized to 0-100; >70 = green, 40-70 = caution (mitigations required), <40 = block unless contractual controls added.
core_questions: What exact data will cross vendor boundaries? (prompts, metadata, attachments). Be specific about PII and PHI.
Retention policy: how long are request/response logs kept? Where are they stored (region/tenant)?
Can the vendor support VPC/VPN or allow on-prem deployment for full data isolation?
Key management: do you support BYOK? KMS/HSM integrations? Is key usage logged/traceable?
Model weights/licensing: are model weights provided to customers? Any redistribution or reuse restrictions?
Telemetry & debug: do they collect gradient/activation telemetry? Are model-training-only signals sent back to vendor?
Access control: role-based access, staff access windows, break-glass policies?
Incident response: vendor timeline for notifying breaches and providing forensic evidence?
Compliance evidence: SOC2/ISO/penetration tests — dates and scope?
Encryption in transit and at rest: algorithms, endpoints for TLS termination, third-party CDNs?
red_flags: Vendor retains plain-text prompts beyond 30 days by default without contractual controls.
No support for customer-managed keys or BYOK when customer data is sensitive.
Unclear licensing for model weights (redistribution allowed) or provenance missing.
Vendor collects model training telemetry that could contain customer prompts without opt-out.
No formal incident notification SLA or unwillingness to provide forensic logs.
Pen test older than 18 months with no mitigation plan attached.
mitigations: Contract clause: explicit data retention limits + ability to purge tenant data on demand.
Require BYOK / KMS integration or restrict workloads to VPC/on-premise deploys for sensitive customers.
Add audit right clause + periodic evidence delivery (SOC2 reports, pen test summaries).
Limit telemetry: opt-out by default for training/telemetry; vendor must provide sanitized debug hooks.
SLA: incident notification within 72 hours + commit to export forensic logs within X days.
meeting_notes:
2024-11-28 vendor call w/ AcmeAI (30m):
- Quick summary: AcmeAI runs a hosted inference service; default logs kept 90 days; offers VPC peering for enterprise.
- Key points: they currently do not support BYOK but have roadmap item Q1; SOC2 Type II in 2023, pen test 2022 (no report shared).
- Questions we raised: explicit request for data retention API, ability to purge tenant, and BYOK timeline.
- Vendor to share pen test summary + SOC2 cert; said they will provide within 5 business days.
- Internal reaction (quick): data retention 90d is borderline; without BYOK this is caution. Likely require contract controls + opt-out for telemetry.
next_steps: Vendor to upload pen test summary & SOC2 report to secure Confluence space (owner: Ethan) - due 2024-12-05.
Legal to draft short DPA attachment: 90d retention cap + data purge API + right to audit (owner: Maya) - target 2024-12-12.
Security to validate VPC implementation and request architecture diagram (owner: Sofia) - due 2024-12-08.
If BYOK timeline slips beyond Q1, escalate to procurement for contract escalation (owner: Noah).
